source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament; complete Acts
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360). Codex Bezae (D/05; 5th c.) preserves Western-text Acts with extensive expansions; for Acts 12 Bezae has several minor expansions documented per verse.
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: P45 (Chester Beatty I; 3rd c. CE) preserves portions of Acts including parts of Acts 12 (lacunose). P74 (7th c.) preserves most of Acts. The 4th-c. uncials Vaticanus + Sinaiticus remain the primary witnesses for Acts 12.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017). Boismard-Lamouille for Western readings.
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Bezae + P45 original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + Metzger UBS Textual Commentary (2nd ed. 1994) ad loc. + Josephus *Antiquities* 19.343-352 for the Herod-Agrippa death-narrative.
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Metzger, B. M., *A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament*, 2nd ed. (UBS 1994). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c.). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + (4th c.). Codex Bezae: Cambridge UL Nn.II.41 (5th c.). Barrett ICC 1994-1998; Bock BECNT 2007; Bruce NICNT 1988; Fitzmyer AB 1998; Haenchen 1971; Pervo Hermeneia 2009; Keener 2012-2015; Witherington 1998. For historical-dating: Schwartz *Agrippa I* (Mohr Siebeck 1990); Josephus *Antiquitates Judaicae* 19.343-352 (the Caesarea-amphitheater death-scene); Eusebius *Historia Ecclesiastica* 2.10.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated in the uncials. Acts 12 contains the chronologically-anchoring death-of-Agrippa narrative (44 CE) — one of the few hard-dated events in Acts.

verses.text: Κατ’ ἐκεῖνον δὲ τὸν καιρὸν ἐπέβαλεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ βασιλεὺς τὰς χεῖρας κακῶσαί τινας τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας.
verses.translit: Kat’ ekeinon de ton kairon epebalen Hērōdēs ho basileus tas cheiras kakōsai tinas tōn apo tēs ekklēsias.
verses.notes: **OPENING — HEROD AGRIPPA I PERSECUTION**. *Hērōdēs ho basileus* = Herod Agrippa I (grandson of Herod the Great), king of Judea 41-44 CE under Claudius. Distinct from his uncle Herod Antipas (the Gospels' tetrarch) and from his son Herod Agrippa II (Acts 25-26). The Agrippa-I dating fixes this episode to ~41-44 CE. Fitzmyer AB 484-485; Schwartz 1990.

verses.text: ἀνεῖλεν δὲ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰωάννου μαχαίρῃ.
verses.translit: aneilen de Iakōbon ton adelphon Iōannou machairē.
verses.notes: **MARTYRDOM OF JAMES, SON OF ZEBEDEE**. The first of the Twelve to die. *machairē* (by sword) — Roman-style decapitation, the standard execution for political prisoners with Roman-citizen status or non-treason charges (vs. crucifixion for slaves/non-citizens, stoning for blasphemy). Cross-corpus Mark 10:39 (Jesus' prediction that James will drink the cup). This is the only narrated apostolic-martyrdom in the NT.

verses.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὅτι ἀρεστόν ἐστιν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις προσέθετο συλλαβεῖν καὶ Πέτρον (ἦσαν δὲ ἡμέραι τῶν ἀζύμων),
verses.translit: idōn de hoti areston estin tois Ioudaiois prosetheto syllabein kai Petron (ēsan de hai hēmerai tōn azymōn),
verses.notes: *hai hēmerai tōn azymōn* (the days of Unleavened Bread) — the Passover-week festival, fixing Peter's arrest to the Spring of (probably) 44 CE. *prosetheto syllabein* — Hebraism (Septuagintism) for "proceeded to arrest" — Lukan biblicizing style.

verses.text: ὃν καὶ πιάσας ἔθετο εἰς φυλακήν, παραδοὺς τέσσαρσιν τετραδίοις στρατιωτῶν φυλάσσειν αὐτόν, βουλόμενος μετὰ τὸ πάσχα ἀναγαγεῖν αὐτὸν τῷ λαῷ.
verses.translit: hon kai piasas etheto eis phylakēn, paradous tessarsin tetradiois stratiōtōn phylassein auton, boulomenos meta to pascha anagagein auton tō laō.
verses.notes: *tessarsin tetradiois* (four squads-of-four) = 16 soldiers total, rotating in the four Roman night-watches (3 hours each). Heavy guard. *meta to pascha* (after the Passover) — Herod delays public execution to avoid festival defilement (cross-corpus Mark 14:1-2).

verses.text: ὁ μὲν οὖν Πέτρος ἐτηρεῖτο ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ· προσευχὴ δὲ ἦν ἐκτενῶς γινομένη ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας πρὸς τὸν θεὸν περὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: ho men oun Petros etēreito en tē phylakē· proseuchē de ēn ektenōs ginomenē hypo tēs ekklēsias pros ton theon peri autou.
verses.notes: *ektenōs* (intensely / fervently) — Lukan-Acts prayer-vocabulary. Sets up the prayer-intervention frame.

verses.text: Ὅτε δὲ ἤμελλεν προαγαγεῖν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἡρῴδης, τῇ νυκτὶ ἐκείνῃ ἦν ὁ Πέτρος κοιμώμενος μεταξὺ δύο στρατιωτῶν δεδεμένος ἁλύσεσιν δυσίν, φύλακές τε πρὸ τῆς θύρας ἐτήρουν τὴν φυλακήν.
verses.translit: Hote de ēmellen proagagein auton ho Hērōdēs, tē nykti ekeinē ēn ho Petros koimōmenos metaxy dyo stratiōtōn dedemenos halysesin dysin, phylakes te pro tēs thyras etēroun tēn phylakēn.
verses.notes: **MAXIMUM-SECURITY DETAIL**. Peter chained between two soldiers (*metaxy dyo stratiōtōn*) with double-chains (*halysesin dysin*) + door-guards outside. The serene sleep-detail (*koimōmenos*) emphasizes apostolic-confidence vs. imminent execution.

verses.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἐπέστη, καὶ φῶς ἔλαμψεν ἐν τῷ οἰκήματι· πατάξας δὲ τὴν πλευρὰν τοῦ Πέτρου ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἀνάστα ἐν τάχει· καὶ ἐξέπεσαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἁλύσεις ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν.
verses.translit: kai idou angelos kyriou epestē, kai phōs elampsen en tō oikēmati· pataxas de tēn pleuran tou Petrou ēgeiren auton legōn· Anasta en tachei· kai exepesan autou hai halyseis ek tōn cheirōn.
verses.notes: **MAJOR ANGELIC-INTERVENTION SITE**. *angelos kyriou* (angel of the Lord). *phōs elampsen* (light shone). *pataxas tēn pleuran* (striking the side) — physical-contact detail, no apparition. Chains drop off. **HIGH LENS-RISK FLAG**: this verse is the densest angelic-prison-escape narrative in the NT and is heavily engaged in heterodox/UFOlogical traditions including the Raëlian canon (cf. *The Book Which Tells the Truth* readings of angel-as-Elohim-messenger). Acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework applies. **EDITOR DO NOT PRE-RESOLVE** toward (a) conventional angelic theology or (b) Raëlian craft-messenger reading; preserve the surface.

verses.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος πρὸς αὐτόν· Ζῶσαι καὶ ὑπόδησαι τὰ σανδάλιά σου· ἐποίησεν δὲ οὕτως. καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Περιβαλοῦ τὸ ἱμάτιόν σου καὶ ἀκολούθει μοι·
verses.translit: eipen de ho angelos pros auton· Zōsai kai hypodēsai ta sandalia sou· epoiēsen de houtōs. kai legei autō· Peribalou to himation sou kai akolouthei moi·
verses.notes: Step-by-step dressing-instruction: belt, sandals, cloak. Mundane practical detail strikingly juxtaposed with the supernatural-escape frame. The instructional-pacing suggests Peter is groggy / disoriented (cf. v.9 *edokei horama blepein*).

verses.text: καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἠκολούθει, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι ἀληθές ἐστιν τὸ γινόμενον διὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου, ἐδόκει δὲ ὅραμα βλέπειν.
verses.translit: kai exelthōn ēkolouthei, kai ouk ēdei hoti alēthes estin to ginomenon dia tou angelou, edokei de horama blepein.
verses.notes: *edokei de horama blepein* (he thought he was seeing a vision). Lukan-Acts vision-vocabulary (*horama* — cf. 9:10; 10:3, 17; 16:9; 18:9). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the vision/reality ambiguity is theologically and phenomenologically loaded; preserve without pre-resolving.

verses.text: διελθόντες δὲ πρώτην φυλακὴν καὶ δευτέραν ἦλθαν ἐπὶ τὴν πύλην τὴν σιδηρᾶν τὴν φέρουσαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ἥτις αὐτομάτη ἠνοίγη αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐξελθόντες προῆλθον ῥύμην μίαν, καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέστη ὁ ἄγγελος ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: dielthontes de prōtēn phylakēn kai deuteran ēlthan epi tēn pylēn tēn sidēran tēn pherousan eis tēn polin, hētis automatē ēnoigē autois, kai exelthontes proēlthon rhymēn mian, kai eutheōs apestē ho angelos ap’ autou.
verses.notes: *automatē* (of-its-own-accord / automatically) — striking adverb; cross-corpus the *automatos* opening-gate motif in Greco-Roman wonder-narratives (Homer *Il.* 5.749 the gates of Heaven; Tacitus *Hist.* 5.13 the Jerusalem Temple doors before 70 CE). Three barriers passed: first guard-post, second guard-post, iron-gate to the city. The angel departs once Peter is on the street.

verses.text: καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ἐν ἑαυτῷ γενόμενος εἶπεν· Νῦν οἶδα ἀληθῶς ὅτι ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ κύριος τὸν ἄγγελον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξείλατό με ἐκ χειρὸς Ἡρῴδου καὶ πάσης τῆς προσδοκίας τοῦ λαοῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
verses.translit: kai ho Petros en heautō genomenos eipen· Nyn oida alēthōs hoti exapesteilen ho kyrios ton angelon autou kai exeilato me ek cheiros Hērōdou kai pasēs tēs prosdokias tou laou tōn Ioudaiōn.
verses.notes: *en heautō genomenos* (coming-to-himself) — Peter recognizes the reality post-escape. *exapesteilen ho kyrios ton angelon autou* — cross-corpus Dan 3:28 LXX + 6:23 LXX (Daniel's deliverance-formula); 2 Chr 32:21 (Sennacherib). Lukan archaizing-biblical style.

verses.text: συνιδών τε ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν τῆς Μαρίας τῆς μητρὸς Ἰωάννου τοῦ ἐπικαλουμένου Μάρκου, οὗ ἦσαν ἱκανοὶ συνηθροισμένοι καὶ προσευχόμενοι.
verses.translit: synidōn te ēlthen epi tēn oikian tēs Marias tēs mētros Iōannou tou epikaloumenou Markou, hou ēsan hikanoi synēthroismenoi kai proseuchomenoi.
verses.notes: Mary, mother of John Mark — identified as a Jerusalem house-church host. *tou epikaloumenou Markou* (the one called Mark) — John Mark, traditionally the Mark of the Gospel of Mark (per Papias apud Eusebius HE 3.39.15) and the *anepsios* (cousin) of Barnabas (Col 4:10). The middle-of-the-night prayer-meeting illuminates v.5.

verses.text: κρούσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ τὴν θύραν τοῦ πυλῶνος προσῆλθε παιδίσκη ὑπακοῦσαι ὀνόματι Ῥόδη,
verses.translit: krousantos de autou tēn thyran tou pylōnos prosēlthe paidiskē hypakousai onomati Rhodē,
verses.notes: *Rhodē* ("Rose") — named slave-girl door-keeper. Named-character detail unusual for Lukan narrative; suggests informant-source for the comic-pericope vv.13-16.

verses.text: καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ Πέτρου ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς οὐκ ἤνοιξεν τὸν πυλῶνα, εἰσδραμοῦσα δὲ ἀπήγγειλεν ἑστάναι τὸν Πέτρον πρὸ τοῦ πυλῶνος.
verses.translit: kai epignousa tēn phōnēn tou Petrou apo tēs charas ouk ēnoixen ton pylōna, eisdramousa de apēngeilen hestanai ton Petron pro tou pylōnos.
verses.notes: Comic-pericope: Rhoda is so excited she leaves Peter locked out. Lukan narrative-art.

verses.text: οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπαν· Μαίνῃ. ἡ δὲ διϊσχυρίζετο οὕτως ἔχειν. οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον· Ὁ ἄγγελός ἐστιν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: hoi de pros autēn eipan· Mainē. hē de diischyrizeto houtōs echein. hoi de elegon· Ho angelos estin autou.
verses.notes: *ho angelos estin autou* (it is his angel) — cross-corpus to the **guardian-angel tradition** (Matt 18:10; Heb 1:14; cf. 1 Enoch 100:5; Jubilees 35:17). Some Jewish + early-Christian traditions held that a person's *angelos* could take on their appearance/voice. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward conventional guardian-angel theology; document the cross-corpus.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἐπέμενεν κρούων· ἀνοίξαντες δὲ εἶδαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξέστησαν.
verses.translit: ho de Petros epemenen krouōn· anoixantes de eidan auton kai exestēsan.
verses.notes: Peter's continued knocking finally gets the door opened. *exestēsan* (they were astonished) — Lukan-Acts response-vocabulary.

verses.text: κατασείσας δὲ αὐτοῖς τῇ χειρὶ σιγᾶν διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ὁ κύριος αὐτὸν ἐξήγαγεν ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς, εἶπέν τε· Ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰακώβῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ταῦτα. καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἕτερον τόπον.
verses.translit: kataseisas de autois tē cheiri sigan diēgēsato autois pōs ho kyrios auton exēgagen ek tēs phylakēs, eipen te· Apangeilate Iakōbō kai tois adelphois tauta. kai exelthōn eporeuthē eis heteron topon.
verses.notes: **LEADERSHIP-TRANSITION SIGNAL**. *Iakōbō* = James the brother of Jesus, who emerges in Acts as the leader of the Jerusalem ekklēsia (cf. 15:13-21; 21:18; Gal 1:19; 2:9). *exelthōn eporeuthē eis heteron topon* (he went away to another place) — famously vague; later tradition variously placed Peter in Antioch, Rome, or simply 'into hiding.' Roman Catholic tradition reads this as the start of Peter's Rome-ministry; modern scholarship is mixed (Pervo Hermeneia 305-306).

verses.text: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἦν τάραχος οὐκ ὀλίγος ἐν τοῖς στρατιώταις, τί ἄρα ὁ Πέτρος ἐγένετο.
verses.translit: Genomenēs de hēmeras ēn tarachos ouk oligos en tois stratiōtais, ti ara ho Petros egeneto.
verses.notes: *tarachos ouk oligos* (no small commotion) — Lukan litotes.

verses.text: Ἡρῴδης δὲ ἐπιζητήσας αὐτὸν καὶ μὴ εὑρὼν ἀνακρίνας τοὺς φύλακας ἐκέλευσεν ἀπαχθῆναι, καὶ κατελθὼν ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς Καισάρειαν διέτριβεν.
verses.translit: Hērōdēs de epizētēsas auton kai mē heurōn anakrinas tous phylakas ekeleusen apachthēnai, kai katelthōn apo tēs Ioudaias eis Kaisareian dietriben.
verses.notes: *apachthēnai* — euphemism for execution (the guards killed for losing the prisoner — standard Roman discipline; cf. 16:27 the Philippian jailer). Herod moves to **Caesarea Maritima** (Herodian coastal capital) — the setting for the death-narrative vv.20-23.

verses.text: Ἦν δὲ θυμομαχῶν Τυρίοις καὶ Σιδωνίοις· ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ παρῆσαν πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ πείσαντες Βλάστον τὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ κοιτῶνος τοῦ βασιλέως ᾐτοῦντο εἰρήνην διὰ τὸ τρέφεσθαι αὐτῶν τὴν χώραν ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλικῆς.
verses.translit: Ēn de thymomachōn Tyriois kai Sidōniois· homothymadon de parēsan pros auton, kai peisantes Blaston ton epi tou koitōnos tou basileōs ētounto eirēnēn dia to trephesthai autōn tēn chōran apo tēs basilikēs.
verses.notes: Tyre + Sidon (Phoenician coastal cities) economically dependent on Galilean grain (cf. 1 Kgs 5:11 the Solomon-Hiram grain-arrangement). *Blastos ton epi tou koitōnos* (Blastus the chamberlain) — court official, possibly bribed. *thymomachōn* (waging-war-with-anger) — hapax; vivid royal-anger vocabulary.

verses.text: τακτῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἐνδυσάμενος ἐσθῆτα βασιλικὴν καὶ καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐδημηγόρει πρὸς αὐτούς·
verses.translit: taktē de hēmera ho Hērōdēs endysamenos esthēta basilikēn kai kathisas epi tou bēmatos edēmēgorei pros autous·
verses.notes: **HEROD AGRIPPA I'S DEATH-SCENE BEGINS**. Cross-corpus to Josephus *Ant.* 19.343-350 — independent attestation of the same event: Agrippa appears in the Caesarea amphitheater wearing a silver garment that shines in the sun; the crowd shouts "a god, not a man"; Agrippa sees an owl and recognizes it as a death-omen; he is struck with stomach pain and dies five days later. Josephus and Acts agree on essentials; this is one of the most secure historical anchors for Acts dating (44 CE). Schwartz 1990; Pervo Hermeneia 310-311.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ δῆμος ἐπεφώνει· Θεοῦ φωνὴ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώπου.
verses.translit: ho de dēmos epephōnei· Theou phōnē kai ouk anthrōpou.
verses.notes: *Theou phōnē kai ouk anthrōpou* (a god's voice and not a man's). Josephus reports the analogous acclamation. The flattery-as-deification trope in Hellenistic ruler-cult.

verses.text: παραχρῆμα δὲ ἐπάταξεν αὐτὸν ἄγγελος κυρίου ἀνθ’ ὧν οὐκ ἔδωκεν τὴν δόξαν τῷ θεῷ, καὶ γενόμενος σκωληκόβρωτος ἐξέψυξεν.
verses.translit: parachrēma de epataxen auton angelos kyriou anth’ hōn ouk edōken tēn doxan tō theō, kai genomenos skōlēkobrōtos exepsyxen.
verses.notes: **HEROD AGRIPPA I'S DEATH — 44 CE**. *epataxen auton angelos kyriou* (an angel of the Lord struck him). *skōlēkobrōtos* (eaten by worms) — gruesome death-detail (cross-corpus 2 Macc 9:9 the death of Antiochus IV; Josephus *Ant.* 17.169 the death of Herod the Great; the tyrant-death-by-worms topos in Hellenistic literature). The 44 CE dating (Josephus *Ant.* 19.351) is the load-bearing chronological anchor for the Acts narrative. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward (a) conventional divine-judgment theology or (b) Raëlian readings; preserve.

verses.text: Ὁ δὲ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐπληθύνετο.
verses.translit: Ho de logos tou theou ēuxanen kai eplēthyneto.
verses.notes: Lukan-Acts growth-formula (cf. 6:7; 19:20). *ho logos tou theou* personified as a growing entity.

verses.text: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ καὶ Σαῦλος ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ πληρώσαντες τὴν διακονίαν, συμπαραλαβόντες Ἰωάννην τὸν ἐπικληθέντα Μάρκον.
verses.translit: Barnabas de kai Saulos hypestrepsan eis Ierousalēm plērōsantes tēn diakonian, symparalabontes Iōannēn ton epiklēthenta Markon.
verses.notes: **TRANSITIONAL CRUX VERSE**. Major textual variant: NA28/SBLGNT/THGNT read *eis Ierousalēm* (to Jerusalem) following Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + early witnesses. Some Western + Byzantine witnesses read *ex Ierousalēm* (from Jerusalem) or *apo Ierousalēm* — which makes more narrative sense (they had just brought the famine-relief to Jerusalem in 11:29-30 and now return to Antioch). The 'harder reading' principle favors *eis* as more original — possibly indicating they returned to Jerusalem before going on to Antioch (cf. 13:1). Metzger UBS Textual Commentary 350-352. John Mark joins the team — sets up the 13:13 desertion + 15:36-39 split between Paul and Barnabas.
